newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil steady to firmer.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil steady to firmer.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil cargoes were steady to firmer on Thursday but both buyers and sellers appeared to be backing off, traders said.
A utility buyer heard bidding at $107 on Wednesday was no longer thought to have been looking for product on Thursday, preferring to wait for lower prices.

Another regular buyer, who was heard in discussions at $106/$107 cif NWE on Wednesday was heard having bid as high as $109.50 on Thursday but failed to buy material. He was thought to have moved his timing requirements towards October.
Offers were heard from a French major.
Regular buyers said a part cargo was offered from the Med.
High sulphur barges traded between $107 and $109 fob ARA.
Low sulphur numbers were steady to firmer although more material is seen available than in the high sulphur market.
September swaps traded at $109.50 fob NWE.
Sources at Swedish private utility Sydkraft said the installation in November of a scrubbing unit would enable the company to burn high sulphur fuel oil instead of low sulphur.
The company has been buying 50,000 to 400,000 tonnes of fuel oil annually, depending on regional hydro electric production.
